types.embedding_query_text: TechnologyCompany: A company that specializes in the development and manufacture of technology products Also called tech firm, software company, hardware company. Examples: Google, the tech giant.

chosen_type.label: TechnologyCompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that specializes in the development and manufacture of technology products
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches the definition and mentions

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: ComputerStore
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of computers and related equipment. Also called PC store, electronics store, computer shop. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer repair and sales shop, Micro Center. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: ElectronicsStore
candidates.comment: An ElectronicsStore is a Store that sells electronic goods. Also called tech shop, gadget retailer, consumer electronics store. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer shop, a mobile phone retailer.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOrganization: An organization that is responsible for governing a country or region Also called government agency, regulatory body, administrative organization. Examples: EU, the European Union, European regulators.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: Law: A set of rules and regulations that are enforced by a government or other authority Also called regulation, statute, ordinance. Examples: Digital Markets Act, DMA.

chosen_type.label: Legislation
chosen_type.justification: Best match for law or regulation

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being Also called individual, human, personality. Examples: Kent Walker, Teresa Ribera, Henna Virkkunen, Zach Meyers.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a human being

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentAgency: An organization that is responsible for carrying out the work of a government Also called government department, regulatory agency, administrative agency. Examples: European Commission, the Commission.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a government agency

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: FundingAgency
candidates.comment: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchInstitution: An organization that is dedicated to conducting research and advancing knowledge in a particular field Also called research center, think tank, academic institution. Examples: Centre on Regulation in Europe.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: FundingAgency
candidates.comment: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A length of time Also called duration, interval, period. Examples: 60 days.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Best match for a length of time

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: MobileApplication
candidates.comment: A software application designed specifically to function effectively on a mobile device. Also called mobile app, smartphone application, tablet app. Examples: "WhatsApp", "Instagram", "Google Maps app", a banking app. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a broader category for any software.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: WebApplication
candidates.comment: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.
